description:
Found while adding fz-5xp.8's fixture.

    dbg([[], [1]])   ->  [#ptr<0x1>, [1]]   Elixir: [[], [1]]
    dbg([])          ->  []

A standalone empty list is the `EMPTY_LIST` sentinel, bits `0x8`. A NESTED one
is a LIST-tagged word whose address is null, bits `0x1`. Two representations of
one value, and `render_heap_value` only recognised the sentinel, so the other
fell through to the raw-pointer fallback.

The rendering is fixed -- both forms print `[]` -- but that is the symptom. The
defect is that the empty list is denoted two ways, so every place that asks 'is
this the empty list' has to know both, and any place that checks only
`== EMPTY_LIST` is wrong for the nested case. `heap_object_word` already
normalises `addr == 0` to `EMPTY_LIST`, so something on the element-storage
path does not go through it.

DONE = one representation, or one named predicate that every reader asks. Find
what stores a nested `[]` as `0x1` and make it produce the sentinel, then the
renderer's second arm can go away with it.

Pre-existing; reproduces at 67e09d373.
title: The empty list has two representations, and only one of them renders
